content: Do not use this product if it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last updated in August 2024. Important Information on Usage: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Common Brand Name(s): Firvanq Uses: Vancomycin is an antibiotic used to treat infections. This specific form of vancomycin is prescribed to treat a bacterial intestinal condition called colitis. Colitis can cause diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, or pain. This antibiotic is effective only for bacterial infections in the intestines. It will not work for bacterial infections in other parts of the body or for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. How to Use: Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, typically every 6 to 8 hours. Shake the bottle well before each dose. Use a special measuring device or spoon to carefully measure the dose. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are also taking certain bile acid-binding cholesterol medications (e.g., cholestyramine, colestipol), take them at least 3 to 4 hours after taking vancomycin. Taking these medications together can reduce the effectiveness of vancomycin. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may allow the infection to return. Side Effects: Common side effects may include abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your healthcare provider. Precautions: Before taking vancomycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this form of vancomycin passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Additional Notes: This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., stool samples, kidney function tests) may be performed while you are taking this medication to monitor your progress or check for side effects. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication in the refrigerator, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze. Discard any unused medication after 14 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
